Defendant Ng Shui-ting appeared in court this morning wearing a green polo shirt, beige shorts, and a black face mask. The charges allege that the defendant, on 10 July and 17 August respectively, allowed a male yellow mixed-breed dog, without being restrained by a leash not exceeding two metres in length, to enter the vicinity of YOHO Mall in Yuen Long, and faces two counts of 'allowing a large dog to enter or remain in a public place'.

The prosecution applied for the case to be adjourned for ten weeks before the next mention, and did not oppose bail. Acting Chief Magistrate Tang Siu-hung agreed to adjourn the case to 29 October for mention, and the defendant was granted bail.

According to the Dangerous Dogs Regulation, a conviction for 'allowing a large dog to enter or remain in a public place' carries a fine of HK$25,000 and three months' imprisonment.

Assistant Director of the Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department, Yip Yin, said yesterday that if the dog owner decided to surrender the large dog to the government, the department would consider options including humane euthanasia; if the owner intended to take the dog back, the dog could be classified as a 'known dangerous dog', and the court could order that it must wear a muzzle whenever going out in the future.

Kent, founder of animal protection organisation Mao Shou Rescue, told集誌社 that the dog owner regretted signing the abandonment form; he also said Mao Shou was willing to take in the dog and provide a dog trainer to rehabilitate it.
